reasons.A: Short declarative first-person present-tense sentences with clipped fragments and a plain, unhedged stance closest to the passage; only 'Not roughly level. Properly level.' leans slightly towards caricature.
reasons.D: Mostly short first-person sentences in the right register, but intensifiers ('every single one', 'exactly', 'gradually') and explanatory asides make it chattier and more expository than the author.
reasons.B: Good clipped rhythm and fragment endings ('A creak. Then a crack.'), but it slides into a second-person imperative manual voice ('Hit it.') and a dry irony ('rather longer') the passage lacks.
reasons.C: Long comma- and clause-linked sentences, a colon and an explanatory essayist tone; furthest from the author's short, stark sentence movement.
